Oliver — thanks for the traffic sketch, that’s really helpful. A few technical notes and concrete starter configs you can use in the pilot: 

Starter endpoints we recommend (Hosted quickstart):
- sandbox.redwood/v1/hosted/chat-sandbox (for early dev/integration)
- staging.redwood/v1/hosted/chat-staging (for end-to-end testing)
- prod.redwood/v1/hosted/chat (we can keep this disabled until you’re ready)

Rate-limit guidance (initial slice):
- Token-rate cap: 50,000 tokens/min per endpoint slice
- Concurrency safeguard: 60 concurrent requests per slice; requests beyond that will receive 429 with Retry-After header
- Burst handling: short bursts (up to 2x) are allowed if tokens in the last minute are below the cap; otherwise we’ll apply token-smoothing

Suggested timeouts & retries:
- Client timeout: 10s per request (adjust if you expect long-form responses)
- Client retry: linear backoff for 429s starting at 500ms, up to 3 retries

Cost ballpark for your sketch (very approximate):
- 45 QPS * 60 sec * 180 tokens = ~486k tokens/min -> ~29M tokens/hour peak
- For a 24h sample window at peak sustained, estimate ~700M tokens/day.
- Hosted cost estimate (using pilot pricing and our quantized model): roughly $0.0009 per 1k tokens -> peak-day: ~$630

Attachments: pilot_onboarding_checklist.pdf (checklist + sample curl payloads)
Curl example:
curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood/v1/hosted/chat-sandbox 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the order history for user 123"}],"max_tokens":150}'

Oliver / team — quick ops note on the hosted pilot and how it compares to Dedicated/Private for your decision: 

Hosted pilot specifics:
- We can provision a sandbox + staging slice within 24 hours of receiving the traffic sketch.
- Retention & audit: Hosted can provide audit logs and 30-day request traces; for longer retention or specific KMS control, we recommend Private.
- Data residency: we’ll pin the pilot slice to us-west region per your preference.

Fallback & canary plan:
- Start with a 1% canary of traffic to the staging endpoint for the first 24h, ramp to 25% over 48h, then full ramp based on latency/error signals.
- If latency > 350ms p95 or error rate > 1% for 15m window, we auto-failover to a compatible model variant with lower compute.

Dedicated vs Private (short):
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and SLA-backed latency, good if you need sustained peaks with committed spend.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full tenancy, customer-managed KMS, longer log retention and compliance controls.

Next actions I can take once you confirm pilot:
- Provision sandbox keys for 2 devs (same-day)
- Enable staging slice pinned to us-west
- Share a short monitoring dashboard link and an initial alert threshold plan

If BrightPort expects to exceed sustained peak of ~100 QPS (or needs controlled KMS), we should discuss Dedicated in parallel. For the pilot outlined today, Hosted should suffice.
